name: Budapest
title: Holidays in Budapest
intro: Steaming outdoor thermal baths, chimney cakes at the Christmas markets and great value for a city break. Here's what Budapest is like, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: Mid-November to the end of December brings markets to Vörösmarty Square and St Stephen's Basilica, with a light show on the basilica's front. May, June and September are warm and good for the river. Winter is cold, but the outdoor baths are lovely in the snow.

things.name: Basilica Christmas market
things.blurb: Stalls, an ice rink round the tree and a light show projected on the basilica after dark.

things.name: Vörösmarty Square market
things.blurb: The city's oldest Christmas market, with handmade crafts and chimney cakes rolled in cinnamon sugar.

things.name: Széchenyi Baths
things.blurb: Huge outdoor pools of hot spring water, steaming even in winter. Some of the hotter pools are only for older children.

things.name: City Park ice rink
things.blurb: One of Europe's biggest outdoor rinks, in front of a fairytale castle.

things.name: Buda Castle and Fisherman's Bastion
things.blurb: Ride the funicular up for turrets and the best views over the Danube.

things.name: Children's Railway
things.blurb: A forest railway in the Buda Hills run almost entirely by children.

faqs.question: Is Budapest good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's good value, the baths are fun, and there's plenty to do on cold days.

faqs.question: When are the Christmas markets on?
faqs.answer: Usually from mid-November to around New Year's Eve. The basilica market sometimes stays open into early January.

faqs.question: Can children go in the thermal baths?
faqs.answer: Yes, but check the age rules at each bath before you go. Some pools are only for older children, and babies in nappies usually can't swim.

faqs.question: Do we need Hungarian money?
faqs.answer: Cards are taken almost everywhere, but forints help at market stalls. Hungary doesn't use the euro.
